item.text:
**Reused Evidence**
I reused only items with a direct AMLO personal-nexus tie.

- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0024"],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"]}`
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0030"],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7"]}`
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0043"],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7"]}`
- `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0037"],"lenses":["7B.8"]}`

**New Evidence**
- Reuters Institute 2022 country report on Mexico: AMLO’s daily briefings and the “Who’s Who” segment. The report says he used the morning conferences to single out journalists and outlets he said were false, dividing media into “good” and “bad.” This is strong contemporaneous context for his public truth-telling style and treatment of critics.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"México","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publication_date":"2022-06-22","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/es/digital-news-report/2022/mexico","claim":"AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps.","locator":"lines 33-38","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"University-based journalism research center; contemporaneous country report with clear description of AMLO's repeated public behavior.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly covers the 2022 Mexico media environment during the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication style; it does not by itself prove falsehood on any single story, but it does show his chosen rhetoric and targeting of critics.","contrary_evidence":["Mexico still had active independent media and public criticism; the report is descriptive and does not adjudicate specific accusations."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"]}`

- The Guardian, March 11, 2022: AMLO escalated against a journalist who had reported on his son by publicly revealing the reporter’s alleged salary, which the article says many believed was illegally obtained from tax authorities. This is direct evidence of intimidation-style retaliation after scrutiny.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexican president lashes out at EU 'lies' over his media-bashing rhetoric","publisher":"The Guardian","publication_date":"2022-03-11","url":"https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/11/mexico-lopez-obrador-european-parliament-journalists","claim":"AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.","locator":"lines 176-178","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reputable international newspaper citing contemporaneous reporting and direct political reaction; the tax-leak implication is reported rather than independently proven in the article.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's response to criticism; the underlying salary data leak is not independently adjudicated here.","contrary_evidence":["The article does not prove the tax-authority leak; it reports suspicion and criticism from observers."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"]}`

- Los Angeles Times / EFE, February 1, 2022: AMLO said his son’s conflict-of-interest case was open to investigation, asked who owned the house and what contracts were involved, but also insisted investigators would find nothing and attacked the reporter as a “mercenary.” This is mixed evidence: openness to scrutiny, but also pre-emptive dismissal and hostility toward the investigator.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"López Obrador dice que está 'abierta la investigación' contra su hijo","publisher":"Los Angeles Times (EFE wire)","publication_date":"2022-02-01","url":"https://www.latimes.com/espanol/mexico/articulo/2022-02-01/lopez-obrador-dice-que-esta-abierta-la-investigacion-contra-su-hijo","claim":"AMLO said the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest was open, asked who owned the Houston house and what Pemex contracts were involved, but also said investigators would find nothing and later attacked the reporter who broke the story.","locator":"lines 63-65 and 87-95","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Wire-based report with direct quotations from AMLO and the surrounding controversy; the underlying allegations remained unproven in the article.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's public response to allegations involving his son and a contractor-linked house.","contrary_evidence":["The article does not establish wrongdoing; it records allegations, AMLO's denial, and a call for formal investigation."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.8","7B.10"]}`

- European Parliament resolution, March 10, 2022: the EP said Mexican authorities showed systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear indications of Pegasus use, and raised rule-of-law concerns. This is independent monitoring, not a judicial finding, but it is materially adverse and directly tied to AMLO-era conduct.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico: The EP calls for the protection of journalists and activists to be guaranteed","publisher":"European Parliament","publication_date":"2022-03-10","url":"https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/es/press-room/20220304IPR24806/mexico-el-pe-pide-que-se-garantice-la-proteccion-de-periodistas-y-activistas","claim":"The European Parliament said Mexican authorities had shown systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear signs of Pegasus use against journalists and rights defenders, and warned that AMLO-era electoral and judicial reforms raised rule-of-law concerns.","locator":"lines 113-120","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Formal parliamentary resolution by a major external institution, contemporaneous with the target year, with specific findings and concerns.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Targets the AMLO administration and its rhetoric/policies; it does not itself prove personal criminal intent, but it is directly relevant to ruler-level tolerance and use of power.","contrary_evidence":["A parliamentary resolution is political monitoring, not a court judgment; it does not conclusively establish personal wrongdoing by AMLO."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"]}`

- AMLO official transcript, March 11, 2022: his government response to the European Parliament called its members “borregos” and described critics as part of a corrupt, reactionary, coup-minded group. This is direct personal rhetoric against critics, not just inherited national media hostility.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"11.03.22 Version estenografica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, desde Chiapas","publisher":"Presidencia de Mexico","publication_date":"2022-03-11","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/11-03-22-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-desde-chiapas/","claim":"AMLO's government response to the European Parliament called its members 'borregos' and described the critics as part of a corrupt, reactionary, coup-minded group.","locator":"search excerpt / opening quoted section","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary transcript of AMLO's own words; self-serving, but direct evidence of his rhetoric toward critics.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's own public speech.","contrary_evidence":["The statement is a political response and does not prove literal falsehood in the underlying EU criticism."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"]}`

- AMLO official transcript, April 28, 2022: he announced constitutional electoral reform to guarantee clean and free elections and to leave behind fraud. This is the clearest affirmative promise in the packet, though still self-authored and later contested.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Presidente presenta iniciativa de reforma electoral; incluye creacion del INEC y reduccion de gasto a partidos politicos","publisher":"Presidencia de Mexico","publication_date":"2022-04-28","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/presidente-presenta-iniciativa-de-reforma-electoral-incluye-creacion-del-inec-y-reduccion-de-gasto-a-partidos-politicos/","claim":"AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes.","locator":"opening paragraph and quoted reform justification","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary official statement; useful for stated intent, but self-serving and not proof of effect.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's stated commitment, but the claim is about intent rather than verified effect.","contrary_evidence":["Later reporting and opposition criticism argued the reform could weaken electoral independence."],"lenses":["7B.8"]}`

- AMLO official transcript, September 7, 2022: he described the “Who’s Who in Lies” segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation and framed critical media as false. This is direct evidence of a state-backed anti-media messaging apparatus.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"07.09.22 Version estenografica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador","publisher":"Presidencia de Mexico","publication_date":"2022-09-07","url":"https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/07-09-22-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/","claim":"AMLO described the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation, and framed critical media coverage as false.","locator":"opening paragraphs of the transcript","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary transcript of AMLO's own words and the official framing of the government segment.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication strategy.","contrary_evidence":["An official fact-checking segment can be legitimate in principle, but the phrasing here is overtly stigmatizing and not neutral."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"]}`

- Expansion / El Universal reporting on the SFP conclusion, May 6, 2022: the government’s anti-corruption office concluded there were no elements to support conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno in the “Casa Gris”/Daniel Chávez matter. This is useful as contrary evidence and as a sign that an investigation existed, but it does not prove innocence.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"La SFP exonera a AMLO, su hijo y Daniel Chavez de conflicto de interes","publisher":"Expansión Politica","publication_date":"2022-05-06","url":"https://politica.expansion.mx/mexico/2022/05/06/sfp-libera-a-amlo-su-hijo-y-daniel-chavez","claim":"The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.","locator":"opening summary and first paragraphs","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Credible Mexican business-political reporting on an official administrative finding; the underlying finding is relevant but limited by jurisdiction and evidentiary scope.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Indirectly attributable to AMLO because the case touched his family and his administration's conflict-of-interest review; the finding is about absence of evidence, not proof of innocence.","contrary_evidence":["The article itself notes criticism that the SFP lacked evidence and that its jurisdiction did not cover foreign transactions or acts outside the federal administration."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6"]}`

- Bloomberg Línea, December 29, 2022: sources said AMLO sought a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and pressured Gerardo Esquivel toward other jobs. This is the strongest 2022 appointment/favoritism signal in the batch, though it rests on anonymous sourcing.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Gerardo Esquivel rechaza ofertas laborales del Gobierno de Mexico","publisher":"Bloomberg Linea","publication_date":"2022-12-29","url":"https://www.bloomberglinea.com/2022/12/29/gerardo-esquivel-rechaza-ofertas-laborales-del-gobierno-de-mexico/","claim":"The article says AMLO was seeking a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and that government job offers were being used as pressure as Gerardo Esquivel's term neared expiry.","locator":"lines 71-86","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Financial-news reporting based on unnamed sources; plausible and specific, but not fully documentary.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within the 2022 target year.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to AMLO's personnel preferences and the government's approach to Banxico appointments, though the sourcing is indirect.","contrary_evidence":["Esquivel had earlier been an AMLO adviser and the article does not prove self-dealing or corruption; it is about alignment and institutional independence."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.9"]}`

- Reuters / Investing.com factbox on Victoria Rodríguez Ceja, November 24, 2021: AMLO replaced his original Banxico nominee with Rodríguez, a public-finance official with limited monetary-policy experience, and markets worried about politicization. This is slightly pre-2022 but matters because the appointment took effect in 2022.
`SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Factbox-Victoria Rodriguez, Mexico's new pick for central bank governor","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2021-11-24","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/factboxvictoria-rodriguez-mexicos-new-pick-for-central-bank-governor-2689873","claim":"AMLO withdrew his previous Banxico nominee and selected Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, a public-finance official with strong budget experience but little monetary-policy experience, prompting concerns about politicization of the central bank.","locator":"factbox bullet list and opening paragraphs","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters factbox based on contemporaneous reporting and biographical detail; the loyalty concern is inferential but clearly stated by the article.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Late-2021 nomination with a 2022 start date and 2022 consequences.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's nomination choice; the competence-versus-loyalty inference is based on the article's framing and market reaction.","contrary_evidence":["The same article notes Rodriguez had extensive public-finance experience and formal economics training."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.9"]}`

**Search and Rejection Summary**
I considered roughly 30 documents across Reuters, the Reuters Institute, the European Parliament, Citizen Lab, The Guardian, Los Angeles Times/EFE, Mexican official transcripts, and Mexican business/financial reporting.

- Kept because they directly tied to AMLO’s own conduct or to a formal finding about his family/network: Reuters Institute 2022, The Guardian March 11, 2022, LA Times/EFE February 1, 2022, EP resolution, AMLO official transcripts from March/April/September 2022, the SFP exoneration reporting, Bloomberg Línea on Banxico personnel pressure, and Reuters factbox on the Banxico nomination.
- Rejected as too generic or not personal-nexus evidence: broad Mexico corruption / press-freedom articles without AMLO-specific conduct, general descriptions of journalist killings, and pure country-context indicators.
- Rejected as duplicative: multiple articles about the same “Casa Gris” episode, multiple summaries of the same Pegasus finding, and repeated media-hostility explainers that did not add materially different claims.
- Rejected as out-of-period or weaker fit: 2023-only follow-ups when 2022 evidence already captured the point, and older background pieces that did not add new 2022-specific attribution.
- Rejected as blocked or weakly attributable: allegations of self-enrichment that lacked a finding or documentary link to AMLO personally, and items that criticized Mexico’s institutions generally but did not establish a ruler-specific integrity nexus.

**Remaining Gaps**
- Direct proof of personal enrichment or hidden financial benefit by AMLO himself remains thin.
- The family-conflict evidence is real but still limited by exoneration findings and jurisdictional limits; a stronger documentary trail on assets, tax, campaign finance, or procurement would help.
- Appointment/favoritism evidence is suggestive, especially around Banxico, but more on other key appointments would improve confidence on 7B.5 and 7B.9.
- More direct documentation of whether AMLO personally ordered, knew about, or later tried to suppress surveillance or media-abuse operations would materially strengthen the obstruction side.
- More evidence on corrections or reversals of specific false claims would help separate rhetorical hostility from knowingly false public statements.

No score assigned.
